## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Mahāhaṁsajātaka* (Ja 534) is a birth story in the Jātaka collection of the Pali canon, titled in English as *The Longer Tale of the Golden Goose* [SuttaCentral]. Set at the Bamboo Grove (Veḷuvana) in Rājagaha, the introductory frame concerns the Elder Ānanda's willingness to sacrifice his life for the Buddha [SuttaCentral; Fausböll 1891]. The story opens with the verse incipit *Ete haṁsā pakkamanti* ("There go the birds") [SuttaCentral; Fausböll 1891].
In an extended dialogue with the king, the goose expounds the ten royal virtues (*dasa-rājadhamma*): generosity (*dāna*), morality (*sīla*), self-sacrifice (*pariccāga*), uprightness (*ajjava*), gentleness (*maddava*), austerity (*tapa*), non-anger (*akkodha*), non-violence (*avihiṁsa*), forbearance (*khanti*), and non-obstruction (*avirodhana*) [Nyanaponika et al. 2003; Thich Nhat Tu and Thich Duc Thien 2019; Tambiah]. In the identification of the birth (*samodhāna*), the king is identified as Sāriputta, Queen Khemā as the nun Khemā, Sumukha as Ānanda, the hunter as Channa, and the goose king Dhataraṭṭha as the Buddha himself [Fausböll 1891].
SuttaCentral identifies the *Cūḷahaṁsajātaka* (Ja 502) as a curated passage-level parallel [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus shows extensive Pali-internal text reuse with its commentary (*Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā*) and closely related Jātakas, notably *Cūḷahaṁsajātaka* (both Ja 502 and Ja 533) and the *Vessantarajātaka* (Ja 547) [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also aligns passages of the text with Northern Buddhist literature, including the Tibetan translation of the *Jātakamālā* (D4150) and *Vinayavastu* (D0001-2), the Sanskrit *Dvāviṃśatyavadānakathā*, and the Chinese *Ekottarika-āgama* (T 125) [DharmaNexus].
